# tfcensus report drift

drift lists the drifted and failed units of a file from tfcensus drift --format json, and
their drifted resources with attribute paths, never values. It runs no plan. It is what the
drift\_summary tool of tfcensus mcp returns.

## Usage

```sh
tfcensus report drift [flags]
```

## Flags

| Flag | Description | Type | Default | Values | Config key | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--from` | drift JSON from tfcensus drift --format json | string |  |  |  |  |
| `--status` | unit status: drifted, failed, clean, early-exit or excluded (default drifted and failed) | string |  | `drifted`: at least one change that no noise rule hides<br>`failed`: the plan failed, is missing or can't be read<br>`clean`: no drift, or only hidden drift<br>`early-exit`: a dependency failed, so terragrunt skipped it<br>`excluded`: an exclude block or a filter skipped it |  |  |
| `--unit` | unit path glob, \* matches / too | string |  |  |  |  |

The [global flags](/cli/global-flags) work with every command.

## Output formats

`--format` accepts `tty`, `plain`, `json`. Without it, the format is `tty` when stdout is a terminal and `plain` otherwise. Formats are described on the [global flags](/cli/global-flags) page.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | The command finished. With --fail-on, nothing matched. |
| 1 | The command failed: a read, a write, a child process or a check failed. |
| 2 | Wrong usage: an unknown command or flag, a bad value or argument, an invalid config file, or a prompt with no terminal. |
| 130 | Interrupted by Ctrl-C (SIGINT) or a cancelled context. |

All codes are listed on the [exit codes](/reference/exit-codes) page.

## Examples

```sh
tfcensus report drift --from drift.json --unit 'acme-live/prod/*'
```
